newsitem.title: USA: Fluor off after Q1, Smith Barney downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Fluor off after Q1, Smith Barney downgrades.

text.p: Shares in Flour Corp fell on Wednesday after the company's fiscal first quarter earnings came in below Wall Street expectations.
Earlier Fluor reported first quarter earnings per share of $0.73 versus $0.68 a year ago. Industry analysts had expected the company to report $0.78 a share, according to the First Call consensus.
Smith Barney downgraded the stock to outperform from buy, a Smith Barney source said.
Fluor is an engineering, construction and diversified services company with an investment in low-sulphur coal.
In its quarterly earnings statement, Fluor said most of an insurance-related credit was offset by provisions to recognize cost overruns at two fixed-price power projects.

"Our entire team is disappointed by the difficulties being experienced on the two power projects," Les McCraw, chairman and chief executive officer, said in the statement. "This feeling is tempered somewhat by the strong pace of new awards and expanding global business prospects."
